findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The documentation matches the design in the context file and the supplied `go-lint.ts` executor. Package lint runs from the edited file's directory against the `.` target. Only the edited file is formatted, and `run` has no `--fix`. Findings carry the package and file context and say they may predate the edit. Infrastructure and stderr warnings are kept alongside errors, an unresolved base or a config the hook can't create becomes a warning, and the outside-root check skips both formatting and lint. I found no errors that block release. The main issue is wording in `hooks-and-skills.mdx`: it implies the edited Go file still gets lint autofixes, but the design removes all Go lint autofixes. Some claims depend on files not in this packet (`config.ts`, `process.ts`, CI), so I couldn't check them, but nothing supplied contradicts them.

`hooks-and-skills.mdx`, Auto-linting section: the general line "Usually nothing — the linter auto-fixes quietly" is followed by "Package lint does not auto-fix sibling files." Together they suggest the edited Go file still gets lint autofixes. The design ("Go lint autofixes are intentionally removed; formatting remains automatic") and `go-lint.ts` (`run` without `--fix`) both show that no Go file gets lint autofixes; the edited file is only formatted. Suggested wording: "For Go, Safeword formats only the edited file and runs check-only lint on its complete package; lint findings are not auto-fixed." The same implication appears in the runtime message's "sibling files were not auto-fixed" (sibling-only wording). That string is fixed by the design, but the docs shouldn't add to the ambiguity.

ARCHITECTURE.md ADR: "Cleanup runs on ordinary completion and handled termination signals" and "real package/config fixtures with the oldest supported v2 and current linter in the CI matrix" depend on `goLintProcess` signal handling and CI configuration. Neither is in this packet, so I couldn't verify them. The design context file is also still headed "proposed design, not implemented," while the ADR says Accepted. Before merging, confirm the signal handlers and the v2.0.0/v2.13.2 CI lanes exist, so the ADR doesn't claim more than it can prove.

`go-lint.ts` always passes `--path-prefix config.base`. When no config is found, the design requires the package directory as the prefix, together with `--no-config`. Whether `prepareGoLintConfig` sets `base` to the package directory in that case isn't visible here. The ADR's claim that feedback names "actual source paths" depends on it.
The "Where hook feedback is supported" qualifier correctly avoids claiming that Cursor displays Go diagnostics. This matches the design's decision to keep Cursor's existing behavior.
